text: Rain rarely stops play in the Algarve, and when it does, don't expect your money back. At the clubs we checked, a green fee isn't refunded just because it rains: if the course stays open, your booking stands. If the club **closes the course** because of the weather, you usually get a **rain voucher** to play the holes you missed on another day, typically within 12 months, rather than a refund. And free cancellation normally ends **days or weeks before** your tee time, so by the time a bad forecast appears it's usually too late to cancel for free.
How often does it rain in the Algarve?

Not often. Even in the wettest months, it rains on about one day in four, and from June to August it hardly rains at all. These are the official long-term averages from IPMA, Portugal's weather service:

text: November and December are the wettest months, with about seven or eight rainy days. A rainy day here means one with at least 1 mm of rain, not necessarily a whole day of it. If you can choose your dates, see [the best time to play golf in the Algarve](/guide/algarve-golf-season-best-time-to-play-golf).

text: **Your course isn't in the table?** For the other Algarve courses, we couldn't find enough published information about what happens if it rains or when you can cancel for free, so we've left them out rather than guess. That includes Pestana's courses (Gramacho, Vale da Pinta, Silves, Alto Golf, Vila Sol and Pestana Ferragudo), Salgados, Penina, Amendoeira, Morgado and Alamos, Castro Marim and Pine Cliffs. If you're booking one of them, ask the club about its cancellation and rain policy before you pay.

Vilamoura Golf spells out how its rain vouchers work. If play is stopped and you've played **fewer than 9 holes** of an 18-hole round, you get an 18-hole voucher; if you've played **9 or more**, a 9-hole voucher. Twilight and 9-hole rounds get a 9-hole voucher. The vouchers are personal, can't be transferred, and those issued in the low or mid season can't be used in high season. You have to ask for one at reception straight after play is stopped.

[Boavista](/courses/boavista) is the most generous on paper. If the course is closed on the day you're due to play, you're first offered another day, or a rain check voucher if you can't make it. If it closes after you've started, you get an 18-hole voucher if you've played fewer than 5 holes and a 9-hole voucher after that. [Monte Rei](/courses/monte-rei) gives a rain check voucher only if you've completed no more than 9 holes, and says plainly that rain and strong winds are not reasons to close the course.

Vale do Lobo, Quinta do Lago, Quinta da Ria and Quinta do Vale use almost the same wording: the club decides when to close the course and when it's safe to reopen, it pays no compensation for the closure, and a voucher is only issued in what they call extreme situations, when the course doesn't reopen that day. At [Ombria](/courses/ombria), play is suspended with a buzzer during thunderstorms and the situation is checked every 15 minutes; if there's still time to finish your round that day, there's no refund. Ombria also suspends play for heavy rain when at least four greens are flooded.
If it's raining but the course is open

This is the case that catches most golfers out. None of the booking conditions we read gives you a refund because it's raining while the course is open. Once the free cancellation deadline has passed, Vale do Lobo says the booking "cannot be cancelled, altered or refunded", and Vilamoura Golf, Monte Rei and Palmares charge late cancellations and no-shows in full. Monte Rei says it gives no refunds "in the event of inclement weather", and Vilamoura Golf, Monte Rei and Palmares all say they don't refund for delayed or cancelled flights or injuries, and recommend travel insurance.

So if the forecast is wet, your choice is usually to play in waterproofs, or to talk to the club before your tee time and ask whether it will move your booking. Some clubs may help, but it's their decision.
Buggies after heavy rain

To protect the course, clubs can restrict buggies when it's wet. Vale do Lobo and Vilamoura Golf both say they can restrict or ban buggies because of the weather, Ombria can limit buggies at any time, and Penina's price list warns that golf carts can be restricted due to weather conditions. That can mean keeping to the paths or no buggies at all, which matters if you rely on one. Ask the club when you check in, or call ahead if you can't walk the course. Our [golf buggy hire guide](/guide/golf-buggy-hire-in-the-algarve) has more.
If you booked through an agency or website

Booking through a tee-time website usually doesn't change the rules: the course's own policy applies. Golfscape, for example, says each course defines its cancellation policy, which is shown when you book and in your confirmation email. AlgarveGolf.net says that if a course is unplayable, you must go to the course before your tee time to ask for a rain check or a free cancellation, and that refunds and rain checks depend on each course's policy. See our guide to [booking tee times in the Algarve](/guide/how-to-book-tee-times-in-the-algarve).
What to do on a rainy golf day

**Before you book:** read the cancellation deadline. If your dates might change, a club with a short deadline, such as 48 hours at Vale do Lobo, Boavista or Benamor, is more flexible than one that asks for 15 or 45 days.
**On the day:** don't just stay away. Call the club or go to reception before your tee time and ask whether the course is open and whether buggies are allowed. A no-show is normally charged in full.
**If play is stopped:** go to reception straight away and ask for a rain voucher. Check how many holes it covers, how long it's valid and whether you can use it in a different season.
**Pack for it:** waterproofs, a spare glove, an umbrella and a towel. Most of the Algarve's rain falls between October and April.
Rainy day plan B

If you'd rather not play in the rain, some clubs have places to keep practising under cover. [Salgados](/courses/salgados) has two Foresight Sports golf simulators in its clubhouse. [Quinta da Ria](/courses/quinta-da-ria/practice-facilities) has a Foresight simulator and five covered bays at its driving range, and [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio/practice-facilities) has four covered practice tees. The Pestana Golf Academy has covered hitting bays too. See our list of [Algarve driving ranges](/driving-ranges) for more.
Frequently asked questions
Can you play golf in the rain in the Algarve?
Yes. A course stays open in the rain unless the club decides to close it because of the weather, and the club also decides when to reopen.
Do you get a refund if it rains?
Not usually. At the clubs we checked, you don't get a refund because of rain. If the club closes the course, you may get a rain voucher to play the missed holes another day, normally within a year.
What is the rainiest month in the Algarve?
November and December, with about seven rainy days in Faro and eight in Sagres. December has the most rain in Faro, about 90 mm on average. July and August have almost none.
